set.body:
Migrated from canardlapin/scalafim Mote bd-01KY5P0R0C44TYYP5PSA8XZP2V on 2026-08-01 after HalfFlow ownership moved to canardlapin/reframe4s.
Source status: open. Source created_at: 2026-07-22T19:49:36.908866Z.

Purpose: place the missing innovation between coarse matching and HalfFlow deformation. Convert sparse correspondences into a confidence-weighted midpoint tangent field, exponentiate it through the existing paired flow, admit only topology-safe objective-improving fractions, and rematch after every accepted bridge step.

Evidence motivating this epic: the verified local HalfFlow-CC engine is fold-free and improves sub18 Dice from 0.89896 to 0.92112, but its basin is about 2-4 mm. The block matcher identified the correct synthetic 12 mm shift, while naive interpolation/application folded. A constant translation has determinant one, so the failure localizes to correspondence assimilation rather than displacement magnitude.

Target algebra: correspondence pairs yield midpoint locations z=(p+q)/2 and tangent observations t=p-q under the existing HalfFlow sign convention. Fit a robust global background translation first, interpolate only confidence-weighted residual tangents with normalized Gaussian convolution and one IRLS reweight, then apply exp(+-alpha v/2) through a group line search. Far from seeds the field continues the background motion rather than tapering toward identity.

Scope rules: retain the current matcher and budget2x local engine unchanged for the first experiment. Interpolate velocities, never finished displacement maps. Damping remains local-objective control; proposal scale responds to topology/objective acceptance; integration depth responds only to numerical flow accuracy. General Gaussian, pull, composition, gradient, Jacobian, and halo operators belong in image. Gale changes require a profiled reusable deficiency; no registration-specific Gale code.

Decisive oracle decomposition: (1) ANTs oracle correspondences to BasinBridge, (2) oracle correspondences to BasinBridge to HalfFlow, (3) current block correspondences to BasinBridge to HalfFlow. Failure meanings are predeclared so matching, assimilation, and fine refinement cannot be confounded.

Epic acceptance: translation and affine-motion oracles preserve near-zero strain and positive Jacobians; forward/reverse confidence is calibrated by ambiguity and cycle consistency; projected fields reproduce constant motion without boundary compression; group line search reduces sparse match error and does not increase coarse true-CC loss; accepted bridge rounds remain fold-free after composition and regridding; oracle decomposition emits a decision receipt; JVM and Scala.js suites pass; multi-pair anatomical claims remain gated on at least five labeled pairs.
set.title: EPIC: BasinBridge topology-safe correspondence assimilation
